decisions.rationale: 'Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome' names one specific disease with a single definition in the title, so the full name is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); §5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: The abstract repeats 'Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome' as the same specific disease; duplicate mentions are each annotated.
'WAS' is the abbreviation of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome in parentheses, so it is annotated as a separate synonymous mention of the disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §6 (synonymous and abbreviation mentions)

decisions.rationale: 'X-linked recessive immunodeficiency' describes a family of multiple specific immunodeficiency diseases defined by inheritance pattern, analogous to 'autosomal recessive disease', so it is a Disease Class.
'thrombocytopenia' refers to one defined condition (abnormally low platelet count) and is a named disease, not a general term, so it is a Specific Disease.
'eczema' is a named skin disease mentioned as a clinical feature of WAS and is treated as a single specific disease concept.
'recurrent infections' is a general, non-specific description of infection occurrence and is not a specific or class disease name; general terms like 'infections' and 'complications' are excluded.
Here 'WAS' is part of 'WAS protein' and refers to the gene product (WASP), not to the disease, so it is not a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (only disease mentions are annotated)

decisions.rationale: 'males' is a gender term describing affected individuals and does not identify a new form of disease, so it is not annotated.
'WAS' in 'severe WAS' is an abbreviation for Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome used as a disease mention in the abstract, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
'XLT' is an abbreviation for X-linked thrombocytopenia, a specific disease form, used as a disease mention in the abstract.
